transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-11
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Owen Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (VertexGrid CTO), Marcus Hale (Eng Lead), Priya Sen (SRE), Tomás Rios (Product)

Optional summary:
VertexGrid is evaluating hosting modes (Hosted API vs Dedicated reserved pools vs Private/VPC) for a conversational agent with strict p95 latency targets for streaming responses. They want to validate token/sec throughput and burst readiness for: 250 concurrent conversations during peak, p95 token latency <= 350ms for streaming tokens, and graceful fallback when capacity is exhausted. Next steps agreed: benchmark run, pricing SKUs, and security docs.

Topics (auto):
- p95 targets and measurement methodology
- concurrency and steady-state vs burst scenarios
- streaming token/sec benchmarks and prefix caching impact
- hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs (SLA, cost, VPC/KMS)
- rollout plan and canary/fallback policies

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for carving time. Quick intro, I'm Maya, I'm the AE supporting VertexGrid, and Owen is our systems engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:07] Lena (VertexGrid): Hey Maya, good, quick morning here. Appreciate it.
[00:10] Marcus: Morning. Jump right in please.
[00:12] Owen (Redwood SE): Great. Our agenda — understand your latency SLOs, concurrency profile, and then talk hosting modes and where we should run benchmarks.
[00:20] Tomás (Product): The big ask from execs: when we roll out the chat assistant it must not slow down the web app. We need p95 token delivery while streaming under 350ms ideally, and we expect peak bursts where 200-300 concurrent sessions kick off at once.
[00:33] Priya (SRE): To add, we run in GCP us-central, requirement to have audit logs and KMS for keys — if private deployment required we need HSM/KMS compatibility.
[00:43] Maya: Helpful. A couple quick clarifying Qs: when you say p95 350ms, is that measured per-token emission after the first token, or end-to-end request-to-first-token?
[00:51] Lena: Per-token after streaming starts, so steady-state token emission latency. But first token should be within 500ms ideally.
[00:58] Owen: Ok. And what's your avg token length and prompt sizes? That affects batching and kv-cache hit behavior.
[01:05] Marcus: Avg prompt ~120 tokens, responses average 220 tokens but can spike to 1,200 for long form. Token sizes vary. Streaming is important for UX.
[01:14] Owen: Good to know. For streaming p95 under 350ms per token, we typically look at continuous batching, small batch windows, and prefix caching. Hosted mode can hit strong latencies for low concurrency; but for large concurrent bursts Dedicated with pinned GPU capacity gives more predictable p95.
[01:29] Lena: Cost will be a factor. We can't blow the budget on dedicated GPUs if hosted API is cheaper and meets p95 most of the time.
[01:36] Maya: Totally — tradeoffs are latency predictability vs unit cost. We propose a two-step approach: run a realistic token/sec benchmark with your prompts against our Hosted ru- and a Dedicated reserved pool replicate. We'll measure p95 token latency, tokens/sec sustained, and tail behavior under concurrency ramps.
[01:49] Tomás: What's involved in the benchmark? How intrusive is it?
[01:52] Owen: Minimal — we ask for representative prompt files and a traffic profile (ramp up, steady, ramp down). We provide a harness that runs streaming calls and captures per-token timestamps. We'll run both variants — Hosted (our public endpoints with your tenant) and Dedicated on a reserved pool tuned to comparable model size/quantization.
[02:10] Priya: For Dedicated, who manages keys? We need to ensure customer-managed KMS or HSM is possible.
[02:14] Maya: For Redwood Dedicated we offer KMS integration and in Private/VPC options we support bring-your-own-KMS/HSM. We'll send the security docs.
[02:21] Marcus: Ok. What about fallback? If Dedicated saturates, can things fall back to hosted?
[02:25] Owen: Yes — we support smart routing and automatic fallback to compatible model variants or the hosted tier; you can define policies like prefer-dedicated, fallback-hosted-on-surge. That does have cost and possible latency implications during fallback.
[02:36] Lena: What's the warm/cold start behavior? We hate cold-start jitter during bursts.
[02:40] Owen: Warm starts depend on keeping model shards hot. Dedicated reduces cold starts because capacity is pinned. Hosted has fast warmup for common models but if a model variant hasn't been used in a while you may see cold times — we use pre-warming heuristics and can configure keep-alive pools.
[02:54] Marcus: When you say p95 per-token, is that measured on Redwood side or we should measure from our app? We need the right instrumentation.
[03:00] Owen: We'll provide the harness timestamps and logs. Best practice is to measure both client-side and server-side. Client-side includes network and edge overheads; server-side gives you just the inference token timing.
[03:12] Tomás: Any specifics on quantization? We're okay with int8 but need fidelity.
[03:15] Owen: We can test quantized variants. Quantization reduces memory and can increase tokens/sec, but sometimes increases per-token variance. We'll surface quality diffs in the benchmark.
[03:26] Priya: Security again — SOC 2, SSO, RBAC, audit logs, retention.
[03:30] Maya: We'll share SOC 2 and a VPC/private checklist. For SSO we support SAML/OIDC and RBAC at team/token level.
[03:36] Lena: Great. On numbers, what tokens/sec are reasonable for a single GPU on your Dedicated tier for our model class?
[03:43] Owen: Rough ballpark for a 70B-ish open model: 6-12 tokens/sec single stream, but with batching you can get much higher aggregate tokens/sec per GPU. Exact numbers depend on sequence lengths and KV cache reuse. We'll validate on the benchmark.
[03:56] Marcus: We have spike tests where 1k requests arrive within 2 minutes, but only 250 concurrent carrying state. We need to ensure graceful queuing and timeouts.
[04:05] Owen: We'll test burst ramps and measure queue times and p95 including queueing vs reject behavior. Redwood supports configurable max queue depth and graceful rejection with priority.
[04:16] Tomás: What about streaming token backpressure? If the client is slow do you buffer tokens?
[04:20] Owen: We stream with backpressure controls; tokens are produced as soon as available. If client can't read fast enough we drop to buffering and may slow production. That's part of performance tuning.
[04:29] Maya: Quick note on model variants — if you plan lower-cost fallbacks we can set a cheaper quantized model as fallback. That may slightly increase latency but reduces cost during huge surges.
[04:39] Lena: Hmm. We worry about quality regressions during fallbacks. How do we detect that?
[04:42] Owen: We can run eval hooks during the benchmark and attach a small eval suite comparing outputs. Redwood Optimize can flag regressions for your prompt set.
[04:50] Marcus: Let's talk live demo — can we get a short demo of latency dashboards and token traces?
[04:54] Maya: Sure, quick 5-minute show. (screen sharing small delay)
[05:00] Owen: (describing) The console shows per-token p50/p95 time series, queue depth, token throughput per model and per route, and a token-level trace you can drill into. You can also trace to request ids and see which model variant served it.
[05:16] Priya: Nice. Can we export logs to our SIEM?
[05:19] Maya: Yes — we have audit export and can stream logs to your cloud logging or SIEM.
[05:23] Lena: Ok, risk assessment: On private VPC do you still provide the control plane?
[05:28] Maya: Yes — for Private we maintain a control plane that talks to your managed nodes over mTLS. You get the same APIs, but data planes live in your network. We can discuss fully air-gapped options too, but that's more of an on-prem contract.
[05:39] Marcus: Good. For the benchmark data we'll share a 24-hour sample trace and representative prompt files. Anything else?
[05:45] Owen: Also an expected SLA target for p95 under normal load vs peak. You gave 350ms per token streaming, first token 500ms. We'll use those as targets.
[05:54] Tomás: Timeline — we need a recommendation to exec by 2026-09-30.
[05:58] Maya: Then plan: benchmarks week of 9/20, results and pricing by 9/24, decision-ready recommendation by 9/29.
[06:06] Lena: Sounds good.
[06:08] Priya: Question: how do we instrument client-side to correlate with Redwood traces?
[06:12] Owen: We'll give a small snippet to inject request id headers and a tracing guide to match request ids with token timestamps.
[06:20] Maya: I'll capture the main next steps and action items.
[06:23] (crosstalk)
[06:25] Marcus: One more: if we pick Dedicated, what's the commit look like? Monthly? Annual? Can we start on monthly and move to annual?
[06:31] Maya: Yes, Dedicated supports flexible commitments. We can start with a short-term reserved pool or a burst-enabled pilot. We'll include options in the pricing sheet.
[06:40] Tomás: If we need to set up a private deployment will there be additional onboarding time?
[06:44] Maya: Private typically has a longer lead — 4–6 weeks for a standard VPC deployment with KMS integration, can be shorter if you provide infra templates. We'll include a project plan.
[06:53] Lena: Anything on data residency? We need EU-only workloads sometimes.
[06:56] Maya: We have multi-region deployments and can pin workloads to regions. For Private we can host in your cloud region.
[07:03] Owen: Final technical note — prefix/KV caching will drastically reduce tokens/sec work if you have many similar prompts. We'll instrument cache hit rates in the benchmark.
[07:12] Priya: Ok. We'll send the traffic profile by 9/14.
[07:15] Maya: Great. We'll run the benchmark week of 9/20. Owen will own the harness.
[07:20] Owen: Yes, I'll schedule and share the harness repo and instructions after this call.
[07:25] Maya: Recap and action items...
[07:27] (Recap)
[07:28] Maya: 1) VertexGrid to share prompt corpus and 24h sample trace (Priya/Marcus) by 2026-09-14.
[07:33] Maya: 2) Redwood to provide benchmark harness and run Hosted + Dedicated streams (Owen) — bench run window week of 2026-09-20, results by 2026-09-24.
[07:40] Maya: 3) Redwood to send Dedicated vs Hosted pricing and burst SKUs plus security docs (Maya) by 2026-09-15.
[07:47] Maya: 4) Post-benchmark decision recommendation and runbook by 2026-09-29.
[07:51] Lena: Sounds good. Thanks all.
[07:53] Maya: Thanks, we'll follow up in email with links to the harness repo and next steps.
[07:58] (end)
